register-long: Five jobs are hiding inside your cash register, and you're still doing every one by hand. One. Receipts. Snap a photo, and an accounting app logs the store, the date and the total for you. Two. Customer emails. An AI writing assistant drafts the reply. You check it, fix one line, and hit send. Three. Your menu sign. A free design tool turns your price list into a clean sign in a few minutes. Four. The weekly sales report. Many point of sale systems can email you a summary every Monday, so you stop adding up columns. Five. Sales tax. A free GST and HST calculator gives you the right rate for every province. Pick one job this week and hand it off. Send this to the shop owner still doing all five by hand.
tax-long: Same hundred dollar order. Four different tax bills. Say your shop is in Ontario, and you ship a hundred dollar order across Canada. To Calgary, you charge five dollars, because Alberta only has the five percent GST. Toronto, thirteen dollars of HST. Halifax, fourteen, since Nova Scotia cut its rate in April 2025. Moncton, fifteen. The same box costs your customer up to ten dollars more, depending on where it lands. For goods you deliver, the rate follows where the order goes, not where your shop is. So set your checkout to charge tax by shipping address, not by store location. And if you ship to British Columbia, Saskatchewan, Manitoba or Quebec, provincial sales tax can apply too, so check those rules first. Send this to the friend who just started shipping across Canada.
receipts-long: Still keeping receipts in a shoebox? Here's a better routine, in four steps. Step one. Snap a photo the day you get the receipt, before the print fades. Thermal paper doesn't last. Step two. Let the app read it. Many accounting apps pull out the store, the date, the total and the tax for you. Step three. Pick a category once, like supplies or fuel, and many apps remember it for next time. Step four. Keep the digital copy. In Canada, the CRA generally expects you to keep records for six years, and a clear electronic image can count. At tax time, everything's already sorted. Send this to the friend with a shoebox full of receipts.
voice-long: This voice model is free, and it runs in your browser. It's called Zonos 3 Mini, from Zyphra. Here's what it can do. It speaks 43 languages. It can copy a voice from a five to ten second clip. It's small enough to run on a laptop or a phone, and a web version runs inside a browser tab, with nothing to install. The Apache 2.0 license allows commercial use, so you could voice your own product videos with it. One rule. Clone only your own voice, or one you have written permission to use. The model card doesn't cover watermarks, so how it's used is on you. Send this to the friend paying for voiceovers every month.
cafe-long: One owner. Zero staff. Picture a café run like this. Here's how she keeps up. At midnight, a chatbot answers the DMs. Opening hours, the oat milk question, whether dogs are allowed. In the morning, online booking has already filled the tables, and reminder texts help cut the no shows. At noon, an AI photo tool turns one phone shot of the new pastry into a clean menu photo. After lunch, every review gets a reply, drafted in her voice and checked before it posts. And on Sunday, a scheduling tool queues the whole week of posts in one sitting. That's episode one. Next episode, the flower shop. Send this to the café owner who does everything alone.
